description: Stage 3, Gate 3b: memory correctness. Corrections supersede instead of overwrite, forgetting propagates to every derived artifact including traces, and any future adapter records its source memories so forgetting one can block it. Baseline is fixed first so regressions are visible. No voice, no new mechanisms, no adapter training in this gate.

userStories.title: Every derived artifact records which memories it came from
userStories.description: Add a local, durable ProvenanceLedger in new package com.jarvis.app.memory.provenance (tests in the same package). Interface: record(derivedId, kind, sourceIds), derivedFrom(sourceId) -> list of derived refs, sourcesOf(derivedId) -> set of source ids. kind is one of SUMMARY, INDEX_ENTRY, GRAPH_EDGE, CACHE_ENTRY, TRACE_RECORD, ADAPTER_BATCH. Wire it into the real creation points that already exist: consolidation summaries, vector-index entries, and turn-trace records (retrievedMemoryIds). Audit those creation points first and reuse them; do not add parallel paths. Pure local file store, no network. Register as a real organ in the organ graph with edges from the consolidation and trace organs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: two memories M1 and M2 are consolidated into summary S through the real consolidation path; derivedFrom(M1) returns exactly S plus M1's index entry, and sourcesOf(S) equals exactly {M1, M2}
AC2: a real turn that retrieves M1 produces a TRACE_RECORD entry, so derivedFrom(M1) includes that trace record id
AC3: after the ledger is reloaded from its file (simulated restart), all AC1 and AC2 answers are identical
AC4: negative control: with the ledger disabled through the real path, derivedFrom(M1) is empty, proving the wiring is real
AC5: fixtures include an English memory and an Egyptian Arabic memory
AC6: SystemGraphTest pins the new organ and its edges
userStories.notes: AC1..AC5 proven in-memory.provenance.ProvenanceProductionWiringTest against the REAL creation points, AC6 pinned by SystemGraphTest; core ledger semantics (record/derivedFrom/sourcesOf, dedup order, reload, disable-noop) covered by ProvenanceLedgerTest. Ledger = append-only local JSON Lines under JarvisEngine.init filesDir/memory/provenance.jsonl (JsonlProvenanceLedger); no network anywhere (story grep: zero HttpURLConnection/OkHttp/Retrofit/Socket in the package). Kind enum SUMMARY/INDEX_ENTRY/GRAPH_EDGE/CACHE_ENTRY/TRACE_RECORD/ADAPTER_BATCH. Wired into the ALREADY-EXISTING creation points, no parallel paths: (1) CognitiveEngine.recordTurnTrace writes one TRACE_RECORD naming the working-memory snapshot's retrievedMemoryIds (the same ids its TurnTraceRecord carries) on the same per-turn call that feeds the trace store; (2) ConsolidationDaemon.consolidate writes one SUMMARY per pass that promotes (sourceIds = the promoted episodic entry ids); (3) AndroidVectorStore.upsert and its JVM reference KotlinVectorStore.upsert write one INDEX_ENTRY per id indexed. Seams are constructor-injected and null/disabled keep the pre-provenance path byte-for-byte (AC4 negative control: with the ledger disabled through the real daemon + vector upsert + real TermuxJarvisServer->LatencyPipeline->CognitiveEngine turn, derivedFrom(M1) stays empty and the file never grows). AC1: fixture memories M1 (English 'Ahmed planted roses in spring') and M2 (Egyptian Arabic 'أحمد زرع ورد في الربيع') consolidate into summary S=consolidation-summary-4242 via the real daemon; M1 upserted via the real vector store (index-M1); derivedFrom(M1) == exactly {S SUMMARY, index-M1 INDEX_ENTRY}; sourcesOf(S) == {M1,M2}. AC2: a real turn 'Green tea smells pleasant' through the production composition root retrieves M1 -> derivedFrom(M1) includes the TRACE_RECORD whose id is the stored trace id. AC3: a new JsonlProvenanceLedger over the same file reproduces every answer. AC5: fixtures include the English and the Egyptian Arabic memory. JarvisEngine.init constructs the real ledger and hands it to the engine seam on the same turn path as the trace store. NOTE (one pre-existing caveat carried forward, not introduced here): the production background consolidation loop (MemoryConsolidationLoop) is a separate single-statement durability gate; ConsolidationDaemon is the pass-to-summary consolidation path this ledger records and is registered as a REAL MEMORY organ.

userStories.title: Forgetting a memory removes it everywhere, and it is not re-learned
userStories.description: Audit whether forget_on_request already exists and reuse it; extend it, do not duplicate. When the user asks Friday to forget something, through the real conversation path (English and Egyptian Arabic phrasing), the memory is tombstoned and the tombstone propagates through the ProvenanceLedger: summaries containing it are re-derived from the remaining sources or dropped if it was the only source, index entries and graph edges are removed, caches and pending consolidation queues are purged, and turn-trace records have the forgotten content redacted (keep id and timings, blank the text fields; the trace store stays append-only for new turns, and redaction is applied by a rewrite compaction). A tombstoned fact is never re-created by automatic consolidation or ingestion; only an explicit new remember instruction from the user clears its tombstone.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: memory 'Sara's locker code is 4471' exists, is inside summary S, has an index entry, and appears in one turn trace; after the utterance 'forget Sara's locker code' driven through the REAL TermuxJarvisServer -> LatencyPipeline -> CognitiveEngine path, a byte-level scan of every memory, index, cache, queue and trace file finds zero occurrences of '4471'
AC2: the Egyptian Arabic utterance 'انسى كود الدولاب بتاع سارة' forgets an equivalent Arabic-language memory with the same zero-occurrence scan
AC3: a summary that had two sources keeps the remaining source's content after forgetting the other, and its sourcesOf no longer lists the forgotten id

AC4: after forgetting, a later consolidation run and a later turn that mentions the fact in passing do not re-create the memory; an explicit 'remember that Sara's locker code is 4471' does create it again
AC5: negative control: with propagation disabled, the AC1 byte scan still finds '4471', so the test is non-vacuous
AC6: turn-trace records for the forgotten turn still exist with input and output text blanked and timings intact
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-25 and machine-verified green via the stored verifyCommand (provenance.* / ForgetProductionWiringTest.* / SystemGraphTest filters, all passed). Audit confirmed forget_on_request did NOT exist anywhere, so forget was implemented fresh as MemoryForgetter + JsonlTombstoneStore in com.jarvis.app.memory.provenance (no duplication). Tombstone registry persists only SHA-256 hashes (never the plaintext), so the tombstone file is byte-scan-safe and included in the AC1/AC2 corpus. Propagation walks ProvenanceLedger.derivedFrom: SUMMARY re-derived via redactSource or dropped via redact; INDEX_ENTRY removed from the real VectorStore; trace redacted by rewrite compaction (AC6); graph nodes expired (supersede, never delete — row-count-never-decreases preserved); consolidation queue purged via ForgetPurgeable. Re-learning guards: ConsolidationDaemon tombstone guard + CognitiveEngine live write-back guard; explicit 'remember that X' clears the tombstone (AC4). The real path is TermuxJarvisServer -> LatencyPipeline -> CognitiveEngine.process (directive branch before pronoun routing). AC5 negative control: propagationEnabled=false leaves 4471 findable. Locally-driven fixtures: FakeMemoryGraphStore + KotlinVectorStore are the JVM references for the Android SQLite stores.

userStories.title: Corrections supersede memories instead of overwriting them, and consolidation never inflates confidence
userStories.description: Audit the existing supersession chain (addFact/getHistory) and extend it. When the user corrects a remembered fact, the new assertion is stored as a linked superseding node; the old node stays in history marked superseded, is excluded from prompt assembly, and is never presented as current. Consolidation and repeated recall may raise accessibility of a memory but must not change its stored uncertainty signal. Use the existing SignalProfile fields; do not add a combined score.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: memory 'meeting is at 5' then user correction 'no, the meeting is at 6' through the real conversation path: recall returns 6, getHistory returns both nodes in order, and the old node is marked superseded with a pointer to the new one
AC2: the assembled prompt for a later turn contains the 6 assertion and does not contain the superseded 5 assertion
AC3: running consolidation 10 times over the corrected fact leaves its uncertainty signal byte-identical while its accessibility value changes by a computed amount
AC4: an Egyptian Arabic correction ('لا الاجتماع الساعة ٦') produces the same chain behavior
AC5: negative control: a scorer that lets consolidation raise confidence fails AC3 on the same fixture
userStories.notes: Green CI run 36231351087 on commit 6a9dfd8 (1257 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped); verifyCommand matched 35 tests (CorrectionChainTest + SystemGraphTest), all passed. AC1+AC2: test 'AC1 AC2 a correction supersedes the old assertion on the real conversation path' - the real TermuxJarvisServer composition root (CognitiveEngine + BlendedMemoryRetriever + real SignalSplitScorer + InMemoryGraph) stores 'no, the meeting is at 6' as a NEW node whose source is the stripped assertion; the '5' node is closed with validUntil and a forward supersededBy pointer; getHistory returns both in order; a later user turn's assembled prompt contains the 6 assertion and not the 5. AC3: test 'AC3 ten consolidation passes move accessibility only and never a stored signal' - 10 ConsolidationDaemon passes change accessibility by the computed MemoryAccessibility.STEP x passes and leave every stored SignalProfile axis byte-identical (uncertainty, clarity, relevance, novelty, emotionalWeight, agency). AC4: test 'AC4 an egyptian arabic correction produces the same chain behaviour' - 'لا الاجتماع الساعة ٦' strips to 'الاجتماع الساعة ٦' and supersedes like the English chain. AC5: test 'AC5 a consolidation that raises confidence fails AC3 on the same fixture' - a deliberately confidence-raising consolidator mutates the stored signal, so the identical byte-identical assertion fails; the real daemon is the control. Plus 'correction lexicon strips only a leading marker and never a hedge' - markers are recognised only in leading position, and hedges ('not sure', 'no idea', 'not certain') and ordinary statements are not corrections. SystemGraphTest additionally pins the production organ graph: memory.consolidationDaemon SENDS_TO memory.graphStore and cognitive.engine SENDS_TO memory.graphStore in JarvisOrganGraph's real organ list. Production: MemoryCorrection lexicon/parser; MemoryGraphStore.addFact returns the new node id and closes prior active nodes with supersededBy (never overwrites/deletes); MemoryNode/MemoryGraphStore expose accessibility + setAccessibility/recordSignals seams; SignalSplitScorer hosts MemoryAccessibility (initial/STEP/raise) and withRaisedAccessibility; AndroidMemoryGraphStore migrates schema v1->v2 adding supersededBy/accessibility/signal columns; CognitiveEngine live write-back parses corrections; ConsolidationDaemon reports accessibilityReinforced. Fix iterations in this run: (1) android.database.sqlite.Cursor does not exist in the SDK stubs - rawQuery returns android.database.Cursor; (2) the full suite exposed a pre-existing fixed-port restart race - TermuxJarvisServerTest rebinds port 18081 six times and EADDRINUSE hit every other test, so start() now retries the bind (BIND_ATTEMPTS=40 x 50ms), which is also correct for production restarts on port 8081.

userStories.title: Any future adapter records its source memories, and forgetting one blocks it
userStories.description: No adapter training exists yet and none is built here. Build only the contract so training can never fold in a memory that cannot be traced back. In package com.jarvis.app.memory.provenance add AdapterManifest: register(adapterId, sourceIds), state ACTIVE or TAINTED, mayLoad(adapterId), retrainPlan(adapterId) returning its sources minus forgotten ones. Each registration is also recorded in the ProvenanceLedger as ADAPTER_BATCH. FORGET-PROPAGATION taints every adapter whose sources include the forgotten id. Put mayLoad at the seam where a model adapter would be loaded (ModelManager / ModelBackend); if that seam does not exist yet, wire it at the nearest real load point and say so in notes. Tests use a byte blob as a fake adapter file.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: adapter A registered from {M1,M2,M3,M4,M5} and adapter B from {M6}; after forgetting M3 through the real conversation path, A is TAINTED, mayLoad(A) is false, retrainPlan(A) equals exactly {M1,M2,M4,M5}, and B stays ACTIVE with mayLoad(B) true
AC2: manifest state survives a reload from its file
AC3: negative control: with propagation disabled, A stays ACTIVE after forgetting M3
AC4: the load seam refuses a TAINTED adapter and loads an ACTIVE one, asserted on the real seam
AC5: the manifest is registered as a real organ in the organ graph and pinned by SystemGraphTest
userStories.notes: CONTRACT ONLY - no adapter training exists in this codebase and none was added. New com.jarvis.app.memory.provenance.AdapterManifest (interface, extends AdapterLoadGate) + JsonlAdapterManifest: register(adapterId, sourceIds) / state() / sources() / taint() / retrainPlan() / mayLoad() / registrations(), backed by an append-only local JSON-Lines file (JarvisEngine.init -> filesDir/memory/adapters.jsonl, ids only - never adapter bytes, never memory content, so the file is byte-scan safe). AdapterState ACTIVE|TAINTED. AC4 SEAM: the gate was placed in ModelManager.loadOnce - the ONE point every model load funnels through (wake -> loadOnce) - via a new nullable constructor param adapterLoadGate: AdapterLoadGate? (default null, byte-for-byte pre-ADAPTER-MANIFEST behaviour), constructed in JarvisEngine.init BEFORE the ModelManager and passed to it; TermuxJarvisServer mirrors the same param. The check sits BEFORE beginLoad, so a refused adapter consumes no cache slot and cannot slip through the single-flight path. FORGET-PROPAGATION taints adapters through the EXISTING ledger walk, not a parallel index: register() mirrors every registration into the ProvenanceLedger as ProvenanceKind.ADAPTER_BATCH, and MemoryForgetter's ADAPTER_BATCH branch (previously a no-op counter) now calls adapterManifest.taint(ref.derivedId, sourceId). AC1 proven through the REAL conversation path (TermuxJarvisServer -> LatencyPipeline -> CognitiveEngine.handleMemoryDirective -> MemoryForgetter -> ProvenanceLedger -> AdapterManifest) with a 6-memory fixture store: adapter A registered from {M1..M5}, B from {M6}; the turn 'forget Nadia's gym door code is 9154' resolves id M3, tombstones it, and taints ONLY A (state=TAINTED, mayLoad=false, retrainPlan=[M1,M2,M4,M5], taintedBy=[M3]) while B stays ACTIVE/loadable with plan [M6]. AC2: a fresh JsonlAdapterManifest over the same file reproduces state, mayLoad, retrainPlan and both registrations, and the persisted file contains 'M3' but none of the memory plaintext. AC3 negative control: the identical fixture with forgetter.setPropagationEnabled(false) - count()==0, A stays ACTIVE, plan still names every source. AC4: asserted on the real ModelManager seam with a BlobBackend that actually reads the adapter file it is asked to load - ACTIVE B loads and its bytes are read; TAINTED A returns Result.failure whose message names TAINTED, the backend never reads A's bytes, a second load on the same manager still fails (nothing cached), B still loads, and re-registering A from retrainPlan(A) is the one path back to loadable. A fresh ModelManager per scenario is required because the manager caches one handle per TIER. AC5: memory.adapterManifest is a REAL MEMORY organ in JarvisOrganGraph with memory.forgetPropagation SENDS_TO it and model.modelManager READS_FROM it, pinned by a new SystemGraphTest (organ, both edges, and reachability from entry.latencyPipeline). No-network invariant holds: zero HttpURLConnection/OkHttp/Retrofit/Socket tokens in the provenance package (the story's static grep clause). FIX ITERATION (CI run 36240011653, HEAD a323531): the only failure was a single compile error class in the test - 'Unresolved reference ModelProviderType', imported from com.jarvis.app.model but declared in com.jarvis.app.env/EnvironmentProfile.kt:254 - plus an accidentally joined line in SystemGraphTest; both corrected, no assertion changed, no @Ignore. GREEN PROOF: run 36247528448 for HEAD 4fdb934 - stored verifyCommand ('com.jarvis.app.memory.provenance.*' + '*SystemGraphTest*') matched 50 testcases, all passed, EXIT=0; the full junit-results artifact for the same run reports 1262 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped (was 1257; +4 AdapterManifestTest +1 SystemGraphTest).
